newsitem.title: USA: NEC unit says US biased in computer ruling.
newsitem.headline: NEC unit says US biased in computer ruling.

text.p: NEC Corp's U.S. subsidiary, HNSX Supercomputers Inc., said Monday that the Department of Commerce was biased in its finding that the Japanese firm was dumping supercomputers in the U.S. market.

"Months before this investigation was even initiated, Commerce, with the approval of then Secretary (Mickey) Kantor, released an analysis finding our company guilty of dumping in order to keep NEC supercomputers out of the U.S. market," HNSX Supercomputers Vice President Samuel Adams said in a statement.

"Clearly, Commerce is not capable of judging the dumping allegations subsequently filed by Cray Research in its antidumping petition in a fair and impartial manner," he added. He said the charges made by Cray, a unit of Silicon Graphics Inc, were unfounded.

NEC has refused to participate in the Commerce Department dumping investigation. The company said it is willing to participate in an investigation by an impartial forum. It has sued the department in the Court of International Trade (CIT) and a trial has been set to begin on April 7.
The court denied a request by NEC to bar the Commerce Department from ruling on the case until after the court decides on the lawsuit.
